section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-18 is code that decides whether a drafted ticket may exist. It runs every acceptance command on main and records the observed exit code, refuses a ticket whose acceptance cannot run, whose files are undeclared or overlap inside the set, whose input and output records are not declared, or whose size breaks the small-ticket rule, and mints ids only for tickets that pass. Nothing an LLM wrote becomes a ticket until this node has run it (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#18-d16-may-an-llm-decompose-work-into-tickets option B).

The rule it enforces was written in rime as R3 and never built: "The architect runs every acceptance command against origin/main before a ticket is cut and records the observed exit code in the ticket. A ticket whose acceptance cannot be run is not cut" (rebuild/investigation/L09-earlier-factory-iterations.md#7-decisions-an-llm-makes-that-a-rule-could-make); five of seven supersedes in that iteration were acceptance that could not be satisfied. Here it is a function with a test.

section.title: Input record: ticket-set.draft
section.text: Kind ticket-set.draft, code 100, from N-17; schema ../N-17/record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket-set.draft. The node reads set_id (equal to run_id), cut_request, source_request, anchor, repo_sha, tickets (at most 15, so a whole set plus its accepted record fits one Commit's record limit, shared/contracts.xml#batch) and verdict_refs. Each drafted ticket names target_node (the DAG node it builds; the envelope's node is the writer, F37), files, new_paths, and acceptance entries with runs_in, expect_exit, regression_guard, test_ref, expected_failure and arch_sensitive.

section.title: Output records: ticket (accepted) and ticket-set.accepted, or validator.refused
section.text: record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket is THE ticket shape of the book. N-03 (intake), N-07 (dispatch) and N-13 (briefs) $ref it and restate nothing; a tickets row read back is the same shape with its row columns (status, phase, row_attempt, not_before, version) filled. On a pass, one ticket per drafted ticket, kind ticket, code 201: a minted id WO-<yyyymmdd>-<4 hex> from id_mint, every drafted field, lane build, status cut, set_id, cut_request, source_request, depends_on_ids, cut_at, and for every acceptance entry what this node saw on main: observed_exit_on_main, platform, classification (guard_pass or expected_match), observed_at_sha, log_path and runs (two when arch_sensitive). Then one ticket-set.accepted, code 201, listing the ids and the platforms. N-03 reads the tickets as new work (tickets.insert is N-03's statement) and closes the cut request by source_request.

On a refusal, one validator.refused: committed envelope plus shared failure_body (ticket the cut request, phase spec, the draft's attempt, outcome refused, failure_kind output_rejected for 422 or schema_invalid for 400), with set_id, run_id, check, reason, the ticket key, the acceptance id, the command, the refusing run and the log path. N-11 consumes it as the spec phase's failure and dispatches spec-author attempt n+1 with it attached. A refusal refuses the whole set; nothing is minted.
On the validator's own infrastructure failure, validator.failed 500; it is not a failure of the draft and never reaches N-11 (#retries).

section.title: Mechanism: the checks, in order
section.text: Package scheduler/internal/validator (planned), hosted by coq-service as principal coq-svc acting as N-18. Validate(ctx, draft) runs the checks below in order and stops at the first failure; cheap deterministic checks run before the one that runs commands. Every check writes one line to the set's validate.log with its name, result and duration.
section.step: Schema: the draft validates against ../N-17/record.schema.json; N-01 already validated it at commit, so a failure here is a defect of two checks disagreeing and is also reported on N-15.
Anchor: git -C mirror rev-list -1 origin/main -- <anchor volume path> must not be newer than draft.repo_sha; else anchor_moved.

Files (F19): every ticket has at least one file; no path is an aggregate (CHANGELOG.md, work-orders/INDEX.md, CONTEXT_STATE.md, generated READMEs) or a runtime path (events/, logs/, anything under the state root); the overlap rule of shared/contracts.xml#claims finds no pair across the tickets of the set; at most 6 files. Every pattern matches an existing path on main, or is covered by new_paths: a new_paths entry must match a pattern of files (else new_path_outside_files) and must not exist on main; its parent directory need not exist, so a brand new package or directory is admitted. A pattern that matches nothing on main and no new_paths entry is unknown_path (a typo is refused, not discovered by a worker).
Records: input_record and output_record name kinds in shared/record-kinds.xml; a dark build's output may be test.proof.

Depends: keys resolve inside the set, ids exist with a status that is not cancelled, dead or refused, and the set plus existing tickets is acyclic (Kahn's algorithm); a go_live ticket depends on its build ticket.

Size: files.count equals len(files); diff_lines_estimate within the draft schema's bound; the set holds at most 15 tickets (too_many_tickets). The reviewer judges concern; the validator checks counts.

Duplicate: no ticket with a status other than dead, cancelled or refused on the same target_node with the same file set and the same acceptance commands; a duplicate is refused naming the existing id.

Accept in one Store.Do under operation key N-18/ticket-set.accept/{set_id}/r1 (shared/contracts.xml#batch): precondition entity cut.accepted:<cut_request> absent; id_mint.reserve for every (set_id, key) (unique, so a resumed mint returns the same ids); ticket_sets.upsert set row drafted to accepted at its expected version; the entity cut.accepted:<cut_request> written with the set_id; the ticket records and ticket-set.accepted. A refusal uses the same operation key with the validator.refused record and the set row to refused, so a set has exactly one verdict: a second, different verdict is 409 idempotency_mismatch and the first stands.

section.title: Running the acceptance commands on main
section.text: The validator borrows a read-only verify workspace from N-14 (role validator, base_ref origin/main, no claims; run_id v-<set_id>) and runs every acceptance command of every ticket by the entry's runs_in. runs_in pod: one podman container on the host from the pinned test image (ci/images.json, N-22), platform amd64, workspace mounted read-only at /work, --network none, no secrets. runs_in host: a transient systemd unit (systemd-run --wait --pipe --collect, DynamicUser=yes, PrivateNetwork=yes, BindReadOnlyPaths=<workspace>:/work), so a host-only proof is run on the host and not silently moved into a container. arch_sensitive true: the command also runs on the arm64 pod path, one pod through the N-24 executor on an arm64 node with the same multi-arch image digest, under the CI admission budget (shared/ci-capacity.xml#admission); both runs are recorded and must classify the same, else arch_mismatch.

Hermetic and writable scratch (C7): every path gets a tmpfs HOME (/tmp/home), TMPDIR (/tmp) and caches (XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/cache, GOCACHE=/tmp/cache/go, npm_config_cache=/tmp/cache/npm) on tmpfs; the module and package caches the image bakes in are read-only and complete, because the network is off. A read-only error on /work or a cache that is not on tmpfs is therefore the command's own non-hermetic write, classified infra with signature readonly_cache or readonly_fs, and refused: the gate would see the same failure.
Classification of each run, in order (record.schema.json#/$defs/classification):
section.rule: the command ran past its timeout_seconds (default 300): refused.
exit 126 or 127, "No rule to make target", or a script path that is missing on main and not in new_paths: refused, with signature tool_missing, no_rule or script_missing.

the output matches an infrastructure signature (read-only file system or cache, network unreachable, permission denied outside /work) whatever the exit: refused 422, because the run proves nothing about the ticket.
regression_guard true and the exit is 0: admitted, recorded as a guard.
regression_guard false and the exit equals expect_exit: refused; a command that already passes proves nothing.

expected_failure is present, the exit equals expected_failure.exit and the output matches expected_failure.match: admitted; the matched line is recorded. A red test that already exists on main must also be listed in tests/expected-red.json (planned; the manifest the gate honours, nodes/N-24/spec.xml) or it is unlisted_red; a test_ref under new_paths needs no entry.
expected_failure is present and the exit or the output does not match: refused 422 wrong_failure_reason; the test fails, but not for the reason the ticket fixes.
a non-zero exit with no expected_failure and no guard: refused; the author must say why it is red.
runs_in is pod and the command's suite is not in N-23's suites.json: refused.
section.text: What is recorded per run: platform, path, image digest, exit, classification, signature, matched line, duration, stdout and stderr tails, log path, observed_at_sha. Commands run in parallel up to seats.json validator_parallel (default 4); the whole step is bounded by seats.json validator_total_seconds (default 1800), past which the set is refused validator_timeout naming the commands still running.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: The validator controller runs on every scheduler tick (tick.scheduler_seconds, shared/contracts.xml#timing): it lists ticket_sets rows in status drafted with no verdict and validates each, at most seats.json validator_workers (default 2) at once. A draft is the only trigger; there is no approve verb. A judged set is never re-judged: its verdict is the operation key's one result.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.what: store reads and the accept Store.Do
wait.timeout: store.commit_ms inside the transaction (shared/contracts.xml#timing); 5 s per call
timeout_seconds of the entry, default 300, max 1800
wait.attempts: 1; a command's exit is never retried

wait.what: podman, the host unit or the arm64 pod failing to start
pull of the pinned test image
wait.fallback: validator.failed 500 image; N-22 owns the pin

section.text: No wait depends on a person.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: A validator.refused is the author's failure: N-11 charges the spec phase (shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner rows output_rejected and schema_invalid) and dispatches spec-author attempt n+1 with the refusal attached; after the third the cut request is dead and one card is posted.

A validator.failed is the validator's own failure and keeps its own retries (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers row validator): the next tick retries the same set after next_try_at, up to 3 attempts; at attempts 3 the record is a defect, N-28 posts one card about the infrastructure, and no seat attempt is charged. Recovery after a restart: the tick re-lists unjudged sets; id_mint returns the same ids for a resumed accept; a left-over verify workspace is released by N-14's cleanup.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Many sets validate at once, each in its own verify workspace and runs. Main is read-only to all of them.

Collision 1, two validations of one set (restart overlap): both send operation key N-18/ticket-set.accept/{set_id}/r1; the same request replays 200, a different one is 409 idempotency_mismatch and the first verdict stands. The loser's runs are wasted work bounded by the timeouts, counted.

Collision 2, two sets of one cut request both pass C6 before either commits: the accept Store.Do holds precondition cut.accepted:<cut_request> absent; the loser gets 412 precondition and commits validator.refused 422 duplicate naming the winner's set. No lease is needed: the store's single writer is the serialization point.
Collision 3, two sets with overlapping files across sets: allowed; N-03 serializes them by claims. Overlap is refused only inside one set.
Collision 4, main moves during C7: observed_at_sha records the sha the runs saw; a command that stops running on a newer main surfaces at the gate with the command named.
Collision 5, id suffix collision: id_mint is unique on id; the random suffix is redrawn up to 3 times inside the transaction.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: A ticket exists with its observed runs. Acts: N-03 (intake, tickets.insert).
The set is cut. Acts: N-03 closes the cut request by source_request.
The draft failed its schema; failure_kind schema_invalid. Acts: N-11; plus a defect on N-15.
A check failed with evidence; failure_kind output_rejected. Acts: N-11 dispatches the author's next attempt.
Infrastructure of the validator. Acts: N-18's next tick, then N-28 at attempts 3.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.writes: validate.log, one <key>-<acceptance id>-<platform>.log per run with argv, exit, duration, stdout and stderr
path.retention: 30 days after the verdict; a set with a live ticket is kept

section.path: Dry run by default; --apply deletes; registered in N-45's cleanup registry as validator-logs.

path.writes: container state under coq-svc's podman storage
path.retention: podman rm --force at the end of each run; any labelled container older than 1 hour is removed

path.writes: nothing persistent (DynamicUser, tmpfs HOME and TMPDIR)
path.cleanup: systemd-run --collect; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-validator.sh --units stops a unit past its RuntimeMaxSec

section.text: The verify workspace is N-14's (N-14.workspace). Tickets live in the store (tables tickets, ticket_sets, id_mint); retention is N-45's. Nothing is written into the repository.

section.title: Permissions
section.text: coq-service as principal coq-svc acting as N-18: Commits of ticket, ticket-set.accepted, validator.refused and validator.failed; statements ticket_sets.upsert and id_mint.reserve; podman run with the pinned image, read-only mount, --network none, no secrets; start transient DynamicUser units (a polkit rule scoped to coq-validate-* units, shared/authority.xml); submit arm64 pods through the N-24 executor; read the mirror. No forge token, no write to any workspace. No seat is involved: the spec-author cannot run the validator; the worker reads only the observed runs on its ticket.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/validator -run TestNewPackageAdmitted: a draft whose files name scheduler/internal/newpkg/*.go, new_paths the two new files, and expected_failure {exit 1, match 'no Go files|directory .* does not exist|cannot find'} is admitted with classification expected_match and the matched line recorded

section.item: A brand new package is admitted (F19).

item.proof: go test TestRedWithoutMatchRefused: exit 1 whose output does not match expected_failure.match yields validator.refused 422 reason wrong_failure_reason with failure_kind output_rejected

section.item: A red run for the wrong reason is refused.

item.proof: go test TestReadOnlyCacheRefused: a command that writes $(go env GOMODCACHE) and fails 'read-only file system' yields 422 reason infra signature readonly_cache, not validator.failed

section.item: A non-hermetic command is refused as infra.

item.proof: probe: inside every path HOME, TMPDIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME and GOCACHE are tmpfs and writable, /work is read-only, curl to github.com fails

section.item: C7 runs hermetic with writable scratch.

item.proof: probe: an arch_sensitive entry yields two runs, platform amd64 (container) and arm64 (pod-arm64), with one image digest; differing classifications yield arch_mismatch

section.item: arch_sensitive uses the arm64 pod path.

item.proof: go test TestRunsInHostUsesUnit: runs_in host executes through systemd-run with DynamicUser and records path host
go test TestAlreadyPassingRefused: exit equals expect_exit with regression_guard false yields already_passing; regression_guard true yields guard_pass

section.item: A passing command proves nothing unless it is a guard.

item.proof: go test TestOverlapInsideSetRefused: two tickets of one set on line/bin/* and line/bin/merge.sh are refused files overlap; two sets with the same overlap are both accepted

section.item: Overlap inside a set is a cut defect.

item.proof: go test TestCycleRefused: t1 on t2 and t2 on t1 is refused depends cycle; a go_live ticket without its build dependency is refused

section.item: The graph is acyclic and go-live follows build.

item.proof: go test TestOneVerdict: Validate twice on one set (the first crashed after the mint) yields the same ids and one ticket-set.accepted; a different second verdict gets 409 idempotency_mismatch

section.item: A set has one verdict and a resumed mint keeps its ids.

item.proof: go test TestTwoSetsOneCutRequest: two sets of one cut request racing to accept: one commits, the other gets 412 precondition and commits validator.refused 422 duplicate

section.item: One accepted set per cut request.

item.proof: go test TestAllOrNothing: a set whose last ticket fails C7 mints nothing

section.item: A set is cut together or not at all.

item.proof: check C22: every example of record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket validates, and N-03, N-07 and N-13 $ref the def

section.item: One ticket shape for the book (F37).

item.proof: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-validator.sh --dry-run lists sets older than 30 days with no live ticket and keeps a set with a ready ticket; --apply removes the first only

section.item: Cleanup keeps evidence of live tickets.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: sets_validated, sets_accepted, sets_refused_by_check, tickets_minted, acceptance_commands_run, acceptance_cannot_run, acceptance_already_passing, validate_seconds histogram, validator_failed_by_reason. The Stats screen (N-40) shows the refusal rate by check; the Alerts screen (N-41) shows validator.failed (infrastructure) and a cannot_run rate above seats.json cannot_run_alert (default 0.3 over 10 sets), because that means the brief template or the make targets drifted. The Machine screen (N-39) for N-18 shows sets in validation with the command currently running and its elapsed time.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See why a set was refused: the validator.refused record names the check and the command; the log is $COQ_STATE/validator/<set_id>/<key>-<a>.log.
A cannot_run on a real make target: the test image lacks a tool; the fix is N-22 (image config) and a ticket there, never a host run of the command to "prove" it.
Re-run a validation by hand: not a path; a set has one verdict. A changed draft is a new spec-author run (N-17) and a new set.
Infrastructure failed 3 times: the card names store, workspace, podman or image; after the fix the next tick revalidates the set without any hand step.
Cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-validator.sh [--apply] [--containers]; registered in N-45.

section.title: DAG edges in and out
section.text: validator.failed goes to N-28 as a defect card at attempts 3; N-18 borrows a workspace from N-14 by a library call, the image digest from N-22 and the arm64 pod path from N-24's executor; none is a drawn edge.

section.title: Sources cited
section.source: D16 option B: the validator's four checks
R3 and the unbuilt cut-check.sh; F-PL3 five of seven supersedes
D01 approve by rule: lint, files field, no contradicted node, evidence method per criterion, DAG input and output declared
F3 the stamp, F4 cut PRs
pod-per-case isolation and the pinned test image; infrastructure retried, assertions never
T04 a verdict the agent can read and cannot edit; T13 enforcement before the model call
set, start, diff, ids verbs: the files field, overlap rule, aggregate refusal, unique doc numbers
the id shape and uniqueness, carried into the store's mint table
the cut checklist: files declared, test plan runs through a repository target, no overlap
dequeue refuses a ticket whose depends_on is not done; carried to N-03, with the acyclic check here
tickets are small: one concern, a few files, a diff read in minutes; every node carries a checklist with proof
a node ships dark and goes live by its own ticket with a named proof
the graph tool's defect; the dependency graph is now rows in the store

item.what: an approval verb with a reason string
item.reason: L11 F3: a free-text field typed by an LLM and no check; the validator's checks replace it

item.what: a graph tool over ticket files
item.reason: depends_on is rows in the store; graph.sh truncated sources on ':' (memory graph-sh-source-colon-truncation)

item.what: banning greps over the ticket's code blocks
item.reason: never built; running the commands is the check

item.source: L13 D01 'graph.sh find shows no contradicted DEC node'
item.what: a contradiction check against decision nodes
item.reason: decisions are rulings in the store (N-29) and the spec book; a ticket cites an anchor, and anchor_moved catches a stale read; a semantic contradiction is the reviewer's judgement
